subject: mass-communication
title: New Media: The Industry
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: New media ventures fall under which category of business?
Which of the following is an example of new media platforms?
Which is used by academicians for research and study purposes?
Which type of businesses started flourishing with the rise of new media technologies?
Big businessmen who lend money for starting new businesses are called —
The first news websites by media houses were launched around —
Customisation of news means —
options: news of one's interest is sent to the user

questions.q: Convergence means —
options: the coming together of different forms of media

questions.q: Most of the early independent new media ventures closed down mainly because Indian customers —
options: prefer to see the product before buying

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Customization of news means whatever kind of news interests you will be ______ to you; new media news stories are kept ______ and crisp.
State true or false: (a) Customization of news means whatever kind of news interests you will be sent to you. (b) News stories for new media are kept very short and crisp.
Fill in the blanks: The ______ of the urban and rural divide is a significant feature of language press growth; new media stories are broken into ______ stories.
Fill in the blanks: Convergence means the coming together of ______, ______ and ______.
State true or false: (i) Early web editions were replicas of print editions. (ii) New media will throw out print and television.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give any two examples of new media.
questions.answer: Websites and blogs (also social networking sites, online libraries, e-learning).

questions.q: What do you understand by media convergence?
questions.answer: The coming together of several media forms such as print, radio, television and new media, which co-exist and are run under one roof.

questions.q: Define venture capitalist and give one example.
questions.answer: A big businessman who lends money to people who want to start a business expecting high returns; e.g. businessmen who funded the new media ventures after 1996.

questions.q: List any two examples of new media platforms where people can connect and interact with others.
questions.answer: Social networking sites and blogs (also websites with forums).

questions.q: Explain any two functions of a website.
questions.answer: It gives initial information to customers and employees through a 'contact us' section, allows feedback through blogs, and offers online services such as shopping and news.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is a website? Write any two features of a website.
questions.answer: A website is the standard new media product, a set of web pages of an organisation or person; features: contact us section with phone and e-mail, news and blogs for feedback, online services.

questions.q: Discuss how new media technologies have opened service-based business avenues. Give examples.
questions.answer: New media ventures need little infrastructure and earn through advertising, subscriptions and services such as e-learning, online tickets booking and tourism packages.

questions.q: Explain the transition to new media in India.
questions.answer: News websites began around 1986 as replicas; the real transition came after 1996 when independent houses started websites funded by venture capitalists; after 2000 most closed and convergence became popular.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the impact of new media in India.
questions.answer: Venture capital funded new media but Indian customers' 'look and feel' preference closed many; practitioners learnt innovative revenue models; technology joined creativity as a criterion and media forms converged.

questions.q: Write an essay on how convergence is changing the face of the Indian media industry.
questions.answer: Print, television, radio and new media co-exist; organisations run all divisions under one roof, earlier forms change for the better rather than disappear, and creativity is combined with technology.
